newsitem.title: UK: Major Euro bourses hit peaks, dollar surges.
newsitem.headline: Major Euro bourses hit peaks, dollar surges.

text.p: Major European bourses got off to a flying start on Friday, hitting new trading peaks after a surge on Wall Street, while the dollar reached a four-year high against the yen.
London, Frankfurt and Paris raced to intra day records in early dealing after New York's Dow Jones average closed on Thursday over 7,000 points for the first time.

On currency markets, the dollar's bull run gained momentum, touching 124.82 yen and analysts said an assault on 125 was just a matter of time. Fears re-emerged about central bank intervention to curb its rise.

Europe's biggest stock market, London, climbed 17.8 points to 4,344.9 on the FTSE index minutes after traders switched on their screens and saw New York's strong overnight performance. The previous high was set on February 10.
"Wall Street's performance was encouraging, but nobody is getting euphoric," said one dealer. "I think there's more (gains) to come, but it will be steady."
He said that over the short-term, many worried that Wall Street was poised for a correction, with the Dow now over the 7,000 mark.
A recommended cash offer from Williams Holdings Plc of 1.3 billion sterling ($2.1 billion) for Chubb Security Plc also buoyed sentiment.
European bourses are seeing record-breaking runs as low inflation has reduced interest rate pressure and the strong dollar enhances prospects for exporting businesses.

But markets will be keeping a wary eye open for clues on the health of the influential U.S. economy contained in wholesale inflation data for January and business inventories for December due at 1330 GMT.
In Frankfurt, shares climbed 0.9 percent on the GDAX index, registering a trading high of 3,260.94 points before easing slightly, supported by Wall Street and the stronger dollar.
But some dealers fretted that a correction in the markets was due and that buying was slackening off. "You get the feeling a lot of funds are already fully invested," said one dealer.
In Paris, shares climbed to an intra-day high of 2,643.98 on the CAC-40 index, building on Thursday's rise of more than one percent. It fell slightly by mid-morning.
Traders said the Dow's push, benign bond markets and a strong dollar were all fuelling the CAC's ascent to record highs. And there were some strong indiviudual showings.
Lagardere rose 2.13 percent, helped by 1996 sales figures. But Renault shed three percent to 126.1 francs, after issuing a fresh warning on 1996 results.

On foreign exchanges, as the dollar headed for 125 yen, analysts said the higher the U.S. currency goes, the more the market fears the possibility that central banks, principally the Bank of Japan, will move in to halt its rise.
"The market is going to carry on buying dollars until you see action rather than empty words from the G7," said Nick Parsons, forex strategist at Banque Paribas in London.
